report.summary: Run detail: picking a run shows its verdict summary, the findings its review round listed, the files it edited and its duration. Run documents now carry the round's own findings and the files a run edited, relative to the project's repoPath, with PARSER_VERSION 6 to 7. Code review round 1 NO-GO (1 High, 2 Medium, 3 Low), fixed; round 2 (final) GO-WITH-CONDITIONS (3 Medium, 1 Low), conditions applied. Canonical run 360/121/304 PASS bound to 123a61c.

events.detail: standard, ceiling assisted -> assisted; ratified earned lift supervised

PBI-014 replaced PBI-011's test_run_documents_carry_no_findings_field with its opposite. The round-1 reviewer judged the reversal legitimate and necessary: that test pinned a scope boundary under PBI-011's F-2/F-4, not an architecture, and the findings ledger cannot answer 'this run's findings' because it keys findings by round ordinal, not run id (findings_doc skips rounds without r['pbis']).

The build first declared AC-82's 'files touched' undeliverable, citing that the exporter reads tool names only and that paths would leak. The round-1 reviewer disproved it at source: the same transcript walk already reads tool input (derive.py:455, :458) and the board already publishes each session's absolute cwd. The orchestrator had relayed the builder's claim to the owner as a recommendation and withdrew it.

The round-1 fix run was killed mid-edit by a usage limit (HTTP 429), leaving the tree failing one test. A second run diagnosed the half-applied state (export_sessions.py never passed repoPath to run_doc; the test was right and the exporter wrong), completed it, and found the interrupted run's parser-version test would have passed without a bump; it re-wrote the test to bite and made PARSER_VERSION 6 to 7.

Round-2 conditions: CR-014-7 (board/local divergence at local/collector.py:436, which omits the repo export_sessions.py:286 passes) - follow-up PBI-027 filed and added to PBI-007's depends_on so the deployment cannot ship with the mismatch; CR-014-8 - the page's wrong claim that worktree edits are 'outside the project's repository' corrected and pinned, with the old wording asserted gone; CR-014-9 - refused or failed edits no longer counted, and ~/ and drive-relative paths withheld. 70 lines over the reviewed tree, change-report-r3.json. CR-014-3 (CLAUDE.md runs row and privacy section must name findings and files) is a close-out docs chore; local/records.py's run shape goes to PBI-027.

The final reviewer measured real transcripts: code-reviewer runs make 0 edits (0 of 37), so for the run type AC-82 names, 'files touched' can only show files its findings name; and 65 of dispatch-board's 140 recorded edits were made in git worktrees outside repoPath, so they show by file name only. For platform-catalogue, main-checkout edits dominate (110 repo-relative vs 10 outside). AC-82 is a demonstration criterion and passes honestly on a review with readable findings plus a builder run; the close-out evidence must state the worktree limitation.

The final reviewer probed the path withholding across another drive, UNC paths, mixed case, the repo root itself, trailing separators, .. climbs, 8.3 short names and /c/ forms; no absolute path leaked, and every value renders through esc().
360 / 121 / 304 PASS bound to 123a61c; base 560e296 confirmed equal to origin/main immediately before the run, and the commit followed the run in the same step with porcelain empty afterwards
